title: Incident Metrics and Evidence Collection Standard
author: Aisha Raman
body:
Summary:

This document defines Redwood Inference's standard for what telemetry, logs, traces, and artifacts must be collected during an incident, how those items should be attached to the incident record, and a minimal metrics catalog that must be available for triage and post-incident analysis. It also prescribes retention, access controls, automation patterns, and runbook changes required to make evidence collection reliable and auditable.

Purpose and scope:

- Purpose: Ensure consistent, high-quality evidence collection that enables fast stabilization, accurate postmortems, and defensible audits.
- Scope: All customer-impacting incidents that meet the incident classification threshold (Severity 1 or 2) across Redwood-hosted and Dedicated clusters. For Private deployments, follow the same standard unless otherwise constrained by customer policy; deviations must be documented in the incident record.

Who this applies to:

- Primary: On-call SREs, service owners, incident commanders, and engineering responders.
- Secondary: Product, security, and customer success during major incidents.

Definitions:

- Incident record: The canonical ticket in the incident management system (PagerDuty/ opsgenie -> JIRA/Confluence incident page) that aggregates timeline, chat logs, and artifacts.
- Evidence artifact: Any file, metric series, trace span, heap dump, profiler output, or config snapshot attached to an incident record.
- Stabilization window: The first 60 minutes after a major service-impacting signal is acknowledged.

Minimum metrics catalog (all services must expose these series at 10s granularity where applicable):

| Metric name | Description | Required tag keys | Alert threshold (default) | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| service.requests.per_second | Inbound request rate to the service | service,region,model | N/A | Use 10s rollup for burst detection |
| service.request.latency.p50/p95/p99_ms | Request latency percentiles | service,route,model | p95 > 200ms (for inference routes) | Breakdown by model variant |
| service.error.rate | Ratio of 4xx/5xx to total requests | service,route,code | > 0.5% sustained for 5m | Split by error class |
| kv-cache.hits_ratio | Inference KV cache hit ratio | service,model | < 60% requires investigation | Strongly correlated with cost/latency |
| gpu.utilization_pct | GPU utilization per instance | instance,gpu_type,zone | < 5% or > 95% | Low utilization may indicate no traffic or stuck processes |
| queue.length | Pending inference requests queued per worker | service,worker | > configured concurrency | Backpressure indicator |
| token_generation.rate | Tokens emitted per second | service,model | N/A | Useful for cost and throughput analytics |

Evidence collection checklist (first 60 minutes):

1. Create or confirm incident record and tag severity, impacted region, and services.
2. Attach automated link to the alert and the relevant Grafana dashboard.
3. Export these artifacts and attach to the incident record (automated if possible):
   - Metrics snapshot (10s rollup) for the last 30 minutes for the Minimum metrics catalog above. Filename pattern: metrics-snapshot-<service>-<ts>.json
   - Traces (jaeger/opentelemetry) covering the time window, sampled at 100% for the impacted route(s).
   - Latest logs from all pods/instances for the past 30 minutes (structured JSON where possible).
   - Configuration snapshot (service config, rollout flags, model variant pinned, autoscaler state).
   - Recent deploy identifiers (git commit SHA, image tag) and rollout timeline.
   - If applicable, GPU health and driver logs (nvidia-smi output, kernel messages).
4. If a heap or native memory issue is suspected, capture a heap dump or native dump and upload to secure storage, then link in the incident record.
5. Note and attach any customer-reported artifacts (request IDs, example inputs, user timestamps) provided by Customer Success.
6. If automation fails, document manual collection steps used and who performed them.

How to collect and attach artifacts (automation patterns):

- Metrics snapshot (CLI):
  - Example: 
    curl -sS "https://metrics.internal.redwood/v1/query_range?query=service.request.latency.p95_ms&start=<start>&end=<end>&step=10s" > metrics-snapshot-service-A-<ts>.json
- Traces export (OTLP -> file):
  - Example: 
    otel-collector-cli export --service service-A --start <start> --end <end> --out traces-service-A-<ts>.zip
- Logs (kubectl):
  - Example: kubectl -n svc-A logs --selector app=svc-A --since=30m --tail=500 | jq -c . > logs-svc-A-<ts>.json
- Config snapshot (git + runtime):
  - Example: git rev-parse --short HEAD > deploy-sha.txt ; curl -sS https://config.internal.redwood/services/svc-A > runtime-config-svc-A.yaml

Required metadata for every artifact attached (as incident attachments metadata fields):

- collector_name (string): name of the automation or person who collected it
- collection_ts (ISO8601)
- time_window_start (ISO8601)
- time_window_end (ISO8601)
- artifact_type (one of: metrics, traces, logs, config, dump, deploy-info, customer-evidence)
- checksum (SHA256)

Sample incident artifact metadata template (paste as JSON into the incident):

{
  "collector_name": "metrics-snapshot-runner",
  "collection_ts": "2026-02-20T15:12:02Z",
  "time_window_start": "2026-02-20T14:42:00Z",
  "time_window_end": "2026-02-20T15:12:00Z",
  "artifact_type": "metrics",
  "checksum": "<sha256>"
}

Retention and access control:

- Incident artifacts for Sev1/Sev2: retained for 3 years in secure object storage (S3 with server-side encryption + access logging).
- Non-sensitive logs (stack traces, structured app logs): default retention 365 days.
- Heap/native dumps, PII-containing artifacts: mark as restricted and apply RBAC-based access; default retention 180 days unless legal holds apply.
- Access pattern: file download requires a signed short-lived URL (15 min) and a one-line justification logged to audit.

Audit and compliance evidence requirements:

- Each incident record must include a completed Evidence Collection checklist. Missing artifacts must be explained and approved by the Incident Commander.
- Quarterly audit: randomly sample 5 Sev1/2 incidents and verify artifacts, checksums, and access logs.

Integration with runbooks and on-call rotations:

- All runbooks must include a single bullet referencing this standard and a short ‘collection snippet’ specific to the service (examples below).
- New on-call engineers must complete the evidence-collection module in the on-call training (game day exercise described below) within 30 days of start.

Runbook snippet example (to be embedded in service runbooks):

1. Run metrics snapshot: 
   - /opt/ops/bin/export-metrics --svc svc-A --start 'now-30m' --end 'now' --out /tmp/metrics.json
2. Attach to incident: 
   - incident-cli attach --incident $INCIDENT_ID --file /tmp/metrics.json --meta collector_name=svc-A-metrics-export

Game day / training exercise (recommended cadence):

- Frequency: quarterly for SRE teams, semi-annually for Product/Platform squads that own high-impact services.
- Objective: validate that automation still collects the required artifacts, that retention and access paths work, and that the incident record is sufficient for a subsequent RCA.
- Success criteria: end-to-end automated artifact capture for the Minimum metrics catalog and traces with correct metadata and checksum.

Failure modes and mitigation:

- Automation job fails: fall back to documented manual collection steps in the runbook and file a task to repair automation within 72 hours.
- Sensitive artifact discovered in public logs: immediately rotate any credentials and escalates to Security; mark artifact as restricted and follow legal hold if needed.
- Missing metrics series: if a metric required by the Minimum metrics catalog is unavailable for a service, tag the incident with "instrumentation-gap" and create an instrumentation task with priority P2.

Ownership and governance:

- Incident Metrics Standard owner: Observability Platform team (primary contact: Maya Chen).
- Enforcement: SRE leadership will review adherence for all Sev1/2 incidents in the monthly reliability review. Instrumentation gaps older than 30 days require an exception or a remediation roadmap.

Change log and review cadence:

- 2025-03-12: Created by Aisha Raman (initial draft).
- 2025-11-05: Added GPU and KV-cache metrics and clarified retention rules.
- 2026-02-20: Updated artifact metadata template and expanded automation CLI examples.

Related artifacts and links:

- Incident playbooks: link to service runbooks and the incident-comm-and-postmortem-framework page.
- Automation repo: git.internal.redwood/ops/artifacts-collector (contains scripts used by export jobs).

Appendix A — Troubleshooting checklist (fast stabilizers):

1. If p95 latency spikes: check autoscaler events, deployment rollouts, and model-variant pinning.
2. If error rate climbs without traffic change: collect traces for 100% of failed requests and sample 1% of successes for comparison.
3. If GPU utilization drops: retrieve driver logs, check kernel OOM, and restart the inference worker processes (document restart in incident timeline).

Appendix B — Template: incident evidence summary (paste into the postmortem):

- metrics_snapshot: metrics-snapshot-<service>-<ts>.json
- traces_archive: traces-<service>-<ts>.zip
- logs_archive: logs-<service>-<ts>.json
- config_snapshot: runtime-config-<service>-<ts>.yaml
- deploy_sha: deploy-sha.txt
- artifacts_owner: <team@redwood.com>
- retention_policy: sev1_3yrs

Contact and escalation:

- Observability Platform (primary): Maya Chen (pager: maya-obsv)
- Incident Coordination (oncall IC): see oncall rota in the SRE team wiki

Notes:

This standard is intentionally prescriptive for the first 60 minutes of an incident to prioritize fast stabilization and ensure later RCA work has complete evidence. Where Private deployment constraints exist (customer-managed logging or retention), include an explicit deviation in the incident record and copy Security and the customer success lead.
